question.text: A trader sells (writes) a USDINR call with strike 84.00 at Rs. 0.20 premium. At expiry, USDINR is 84.75. What is the writer's net P&L per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: A short-call writer's payoff is the mirror image of the long-call buyer: premium received minus the intrinsic payoff to the buyer. Here writer P&L = 0.20 - max(84.75 - 84.00, 0) = 0.20 - 0.75 = -Rs. 0.55 per unit. Using the 1000 USD lot size, this is Rs. 550 loss per lot and the maximum profit equals the premium received, Rs. 200 per lot. The Trap: Rs. 0.75 is the buyer's gross intrinsic payoff and ignores the premium the writer collected upfront; the writer's loss is offset by that premium. Note: Workbook reference — pp.82-83 (short-call payoff as mirror of long call, with payoff table values consistent with premium received minus intrinsic payoff).
